It was insinuating by the camera, if this was broadcast, that these were, in fact, guilty people. And I said, Okay, let's try to maybe remove the cameras. The cameras, as were described, as I recall it, by General Cermak, were for internal use or Croatian authority use only. I recall seeing that this was not just the private or Croatian authority video unit, but an emblem on the camera of a Croatian TV station. And that was why I was not annoyed, but I just thought, Okay. Well, we can go and film for our record of the UN on record on tape the UN TV's record of a Croatian TV crew filming suspected war crimes suspects going on the bus. And my colleagues from UN TV went and did this, it was all over in about 20 seconds, and they came back inside the gates. As they came back in inside, I recall that General Cermak was not entirely happy, to put it politely, and did say to me words to the effect that this was seen as provocation, was not helpful, and words were directed to me directly in terms of my behaviour, to put it politely. I can say this. I can understand it was a very pressurised moment, but I did not on the specific issue think it right that the TV crew should film in the way that it was, and this was the only reason I persuaded or suggested the UN TV crew might film what was happening from inside the gates, and then to go out and film by the bus doorway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So what purpose did your filming the Croatians serve? It's not immediately apparent.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS
utterances.text: The filming stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What purpose --

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS
utterances.text: The filming by the Croatian TV crew of those going through the gates to the bus stopped shortly after the UN TV crew began filming them, because it was a record of what I thought was in terms of the conduct of a government authority to act properly at the time it was receiving persons who had allegedly committed serious crimes, in this case war crimes. But there is, I think, a professional conduct expected. And to my mind and I know from my colleague EJ Flynn and from UNHCR colleagues there at the gates, this was thought of as not being proper. And that was the reason we did this with the UN TV. And UN TV inside the gates of Sector South are entitled to film on UN property what was before them, but they were not doing that until that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What's it for you to decide whether the Croatian government should tape these steps or not? There are a number of readily apparent reasons as to why suspects coming from the custody or coming from the place of one party into the custody of another party may want to film their condition, what they looked like, and their identities. Can't you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS
utterances.text: Oh, I can see it very well, sir, and I think that that kind of behaviour, not just from myself but from others who have got more expertise in international humanitarian law who were inside the UN Sector South, not just Sector South personnel but those sent down from headquarters Zagreb, were of the same clear opinion, that this was one step beyond what was appropriate behaviour. And in my experience later in Bosnia-Herzegovina on the issue of war crimes suspects, I had never seen or never saw that kind of behaviour again from a local TV crew in the presence of their respective local or government authorities acting in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, you don't know whether they were a local TV crew and you don't know what purposes the recording was for, do you?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS
utterances.text: I would suspect, sir, that if it's a UN -- if it's a Croatian television broadcasting company, that they are filming a report for what would be news TV purposes. If they were going to be producing a film to hand it over for the Croatian authorities, then one would suspect that they are not a legitimate TV organization. But on the actual camera back was the logo of a TV station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you ask? Did you ask?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS
utterances.text: Did I ask the TV crew?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you ask why it was happening?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS
utterances.text: No, because there was a lot of activity at the front of the gates and a very sensitive situation. I decided, once the actual situation had subsided with the TV crew filming face on the faces of the people entering the buses, that that had stopped. They moved away, they did not seem angry with the UN TV crew or EJ Flynn or myself, and they just stopped filming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And what was your business as a press and information officer to start interfering in a delicately arranged matter between the United Nations and the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS
utterances.text: Well, sir, I was not interfering, and that was not what I did on that evening at all. The process by which long negotiations between the Croatian government authorities and the UN mission at Zagreb headquarters had concluded were ongoing. This is one particular specific incident that occurred, and not only myself but others there from UN human rights, from mission headquarters Zagreb felt this was inappropriate. And our UN TV crew could have also been filming away what, I think, was quite a sensitive situation did not do so because we thought it was quite inappropriate to film and, therefore, stepped-up to make that small gesture or shot at the time that they happened. It was all over within about 20 seconds or less, as I stated in my statement of 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, could we move on. We've now spent quite some time on what moved, how one moved to film one way, and what moved another one to film the ones filming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that seems not to be the core of this case. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware, in fact, that the UNCRO had written to the Ministry of Defence of the Government of Croatia, Exhibit D316, about the transport of refugees being carried out in accordance with the UNCRO and Sector South commander's plan and various international organizations from Sector South and other agency took part. One of the key persons of success of this mission was Colonel-General Cermak, liaison officers Captain Lukovic, Mrsa, and Dondo. And General Cermak was congratulated by Colonel Blahna for quick and professional arrangements.

utterances.speaker: ALUN ROBERTS
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen this letter before and I've seen it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've finished this matter, and I note the time and rather than start a new subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the parties give any indication as to the time still needed with Mr. Roberts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would have from my original time estimate no longer than two hours before I finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The other Defence counsel. Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll be up next and I will estimate two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That makes four. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Obviously, depending on what happens in front of me, Judge, but I would say four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would mean that it would take us two more days. Mr. Roberts, did I hear a sigh or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, not at all. No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's good. We adjourn for the day. We will resume tomorrow morning, 9.00. But I'd first like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether the testimony you gave already today or testimony still to be given in days to come. Madam Registrar, we resume tomorrow at 9.00 in this same courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be, unfortunately, in Courtroom II, tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 22nd day of July, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
